**Tafsir of Surah al-Qiyamah**

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

It has been mentioned more than once that when the thing sworn about is negated, the particle *la* (no) may be placed before the oath to emphasise the negation. The thing sworn about here is the affirmation of the appointed Day (*al-mi'ad*), and the refutation of what the ignorant among the servants claim, namely that bodies will not be resurrected. For this reason, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul.﴾ Al-Hasan said: "He swore by the Day of Resurrection and did not swear by the self-reproaching soul." Qatadah said: "Rather, He swore by both of them together." Thus [it is] related by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir has related from al-Hasan and al-A'raj that they both read: "La-uqsimu [bi-yawm al-qiyamah]" (I swear by the Day of Resurrection). [In manuscript M: "Thus." Addition from manuscript M.] This supports al-Hasan's view, since it affirms the oath by the Day of Resurrection and negates the oath by the self-reproaching soul. The correct view, however, is that He swore by both of them together, as Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said. This is also what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and it is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

As for the Day of Resurrection, it is well known. As for the self-reproaching soul, Qurrah ibn Khalid related from al-Hasan al-Basri concerning this verse: "Indeed, the believer, by Allah, we see him only blaming himself: 'What did I intend by my words? What did I intend by my food? What did I intend by the thoughts of my soul?' But the wicked one proceeds onward without rebuking himself."

Juwaybir said: "It reached us from al-Hasan that he said, concerning His words: ﴿And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾: 'No one from among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth but will blame himself on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "My father related to us: 'Abdullah ibn Salih ibn [In manuscript M: "from"] Muslim related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak: that he asked Ikrimah about His words: ﴿And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾. He said: 'It blames [In manuscript M: "you blame"] for good and evil: "If only I had done such and such."'"

This was also related by Ibn Jarir, from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', from Isra'il.

Ibn Jarir said: "Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Mu'ammal related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning: ﴿And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾: 'It blames for good and evil.'"

Then he related it through another chain from Sa'id, that he asked Ibn 'Abbas about it, and he said: "It is the blaming soul (*al-nafs al-lu'ama*)."

'Ali ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "It regrets what has passed and blames itself for it."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "*Al-lawwamah*: the blameworthy one."

Qatadah said: "*Al-lawwamah*: the wicked one."

Ibn Jarir said: "All these sayings are close in meaning. The most apparent in the wording of the revelation is that it is the soul that blames its owner for good and evil and regrets what has passed."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection: does he suppose that We are not able to restore his bones and gather them from their scattered places? ﴿Yes, [We are] able to put together even his fingertips.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "That We would make it [In manuscript A: "that We would transform it"] a hoof or a hoofed foot." Similarly said Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir explained it by saying that if He wished, He would have made that [capability] in this world.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that His words ﴿able﴾ are a circumstantial clause (*hal*) relating to His words ﴿assemble﴾. That is: does man suppose that We do not assemble his bones? Rather, We will assemble them, being able to put together his fingertips; that is, Our power is sufficient to assemble them, and if We wished, We would resurrect him even more perfectly than he was, making his fingertips, which are the extremities of his fingers, level and well-formed. This is the meaning given by Ibn Qutaybah and al-Zajjaj.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Rather, man wants to continue in wickedness ahead of him.﴾ Sa'id related from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, he proceeds onward."

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿to continue in wickedness ahead of him﴾ means: the hope [of a long life]. The person says: "I will act, then I will repent before the Day of Resurrection." It is also said that it means: disbelief in the truth before the Day of Resurrection.

Mujahid said: ﴿to continue in wickedness ahead of him﴾: to proceed ahead, riding his head [in defiance]. Al-Hasan said: "No son of Adam meets Allah except that his soul inclines toward disobedience of Allah, onward and onward, except those whom Allah protects."

It is related from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and many of the early scholars (*salaf*): it is the one who hastens sins and procrastinates repentance.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is the disbeliever who denies the Day of Reckoning." Ibn Zayd said likewise, and this is the most apparent meaning. For this reason He said after it: ﴿He asks: When is the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is, he says: when will the Day of Resurrection occur? His question is one of deeming its occurrence remote and denying its existence, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they say: "When is this promise, if you are truthful?" Say: "For you is an appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay an hour, nor can you advance it."﴾ [Saba': 29–30].

Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿So when the sight is dazzled.﴾ Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "*Baraqa* with a kasra on the *ra*," that is, it was bewildered. What he said resembles the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Their gaze does not return to them﴾ [Ibrahim: 43], rather they look about in terror, this way and that, with no gaze settling on anything, from the intensity of dread.

Others read: "*Baraqa*" with a fatha, and in meaning it is close to the first. The intended meaning is that sight will be overwhelmed on the Day of Resurrection, humbled, bewildered and abased from the intensity of the terrors and the greatness of what is witnessed on that Day.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And the moon is eclipsed﴾, that is: its light departs.

﴿And the sun and the moon are joined﴾. Mujahid said: "They are folded up (*kuwwira*)." Ibn Zayd, when explaining this verse, recited: ﴿When the sun is folded up, and when the stars fall﴾ [At-Takwir: 1–2]. It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he read: "*Wa-judi'a bayna al-shamsi wal-qamar*" (And the sun and moon were brought together).

* *

As for His words: ﴿The human will say on that Day, "Where is the escape?"﴾ That is, when the son of Adam witnesses these terrors on the Day of Resurrection, at that time he will desire to flee and say: "Where is the escape?" That is: is there any refuge or shelter? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No! There is no refuge. To your Lord, that Day, is the place of rest.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and many of the early scholars said: that is, there is no salvation.

This is like His words: ﴿You will have no refuge that Day, nor will you have any place to deny [your sins]﴾ [Ash-Shura: 47], that is: you will have no place in which you can hide yourselves. Likewise He says here: ﴿There is no refuge﴾, that is: you will have no place in which you can seek protection. For this reason He said: ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the place of rest﴾, that is: the return and the final destination.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾, that is: he will be told of all his deeds, the earlier and the later, the first and the last, the small and the great, just as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf: 49]. Likewise He says here: ﴿Rather, man is, against himself, a witness, even if he presents his excuses﴾, that is: he is a witness against himself, knowing what he did even if he makes excuses and denies it, just as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is your soul against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra': 14].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Rather, man is, against himself, a witness﴾: his hearing, his sight, his hands, his feet, and his limbs [will testify against him].

Qatadah said: "He is a witness against himself." In another narration he said: "If you wish, by Allah, you will see him perceptive of the faults and sins of people, but heedless of his own sins." It used to be said: "In the Gospel it is written: 'O son of Adam, you see the speck in your brother's eye, but you leave the trunk in your own eye unseen.'" [In manuscript M: "and you leave the trunk"]

Mujahid said: ﴿even if he presents his excuses﴾: even if he argues on their behalf, he is a witness against them. Qatadah said: ﴿even if he presents his excuses﴾: even if he makes excuses that day with falsehood, it will not be accepted from him. As-Suddi said: ﴿even if he presents his excuses﴾: his argument. Likewise said Ibn Zayd, al-Hasan al-Basri, and others, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Qatadah related from Zurarah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿even if he presents his excuses﴾: he says: even if he throws down his garments.

Ad-Dahhak said: "Even if he lets down his curtains." The people of Yemen call the curtain *al-mi'dhar*.

The correct view is the saying of Mujahid and his companions, like His words: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am: 23], and like His words: ﴿The Day when Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 18].

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿even if he presents his excuses﴾: it is the making of excuses. Have you not heard that He said: ﴿The excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them﴾ [Ghafir: 52], and He said: ﴿And they will submit to Allah that Day﴾ [An-Nahl: 87], ﴿Then they will submit [their] surrender: "We did not do any evil"﴾ [An-Nahl: 28], and their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾.

If we take it to mean (ḥaqqan) "truly", it is clear: truly, when it reaches the collarbones, that is, when your soul is pulled out of your body and reaches your collarbones. The "tarāqī" (collarbones) is the plural of "tarqūwah" (collarbone), which are the bones between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder, as in His saying: ﴿Then why not, when it reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on? And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. Then why not, if you are not to be judged, you bring it back, if you should be truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Nay! When it reaches the collarbones﴾. And here the ḥadīth of Busr ibn Jaḥsh is mentioned, which was preceded in the commentary on Surah Yasin [[The ḥadīth of Busr ibn Jaḥsh, narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/310) through Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Busr ibn Jaḥsh: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spat one day into his palm, then placed his finger upon it, then said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: O son of Adam, do you think you can frustrate Me when I created you like this, until when I had proportioned you and balanced you, you walked between your two garments while the earth was yours to tread, then you gathered and withheld, until when the collarbones reached [the throat] you said: 'Shall I give charity? And when is the time for charity?!'" This was previously mentioned in the commentary on verse 77 of Surah Yasin.]]. The "tarāqī" is the plural of "tarqūwah", which is close to the throat (ḥulqūm).

﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, who is one who will perform ruqyah (incantation for healing)? Likewise Abu Qilabah said: ﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ meaning: who is a physician who can heal? Likewise said Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Rawh ibn al-Musayyib Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ He said: It is said: who will ascend with his soul: the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment? According to this, it is from the speech of the angels.

With this same chain, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾ he said: the world and the Hereafter are wound around him. Likewise said Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾ says: the last day of the world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter, so hardship meets hardship, except for those whom Allah has mercy upon.

Ikrimah said: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾: a great matter with a great matter. Mujahid said: affliction with affliction. Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾, said: they are your two legs when they are wound together. In another narration from him: his two legs die and do not carry him, though he used to walk upon them. Likewise said al-Suddi, from Abu Malik.

In another narration from al-Hasan: it is the wrapping of the two of them in the shroud.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾: two matters gather upon him: people prepare his body, and the angels prepare his soul.

* *

His saying: ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾, that is, the return and the place of return. This is because the soul is raised to the heavens, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Return My servant to the earth, for from it I created them, into it I will return them, and from it I will bring them out once more." As occurs in the lengthy ḥadīth of al-Bara'. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ [al-An'am: 61–62].

* *

His saying: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away﴾ This is information about the disbeliever who, in the worldly life, denied the truth in his heart and turned away from acting with his body, so there is no good in him, inwardly or outwardly. For this reason He said: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾, that is: exultant, insolent, arrogant, lazy, having no resolve and no deed, as He said: ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 31]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, he was among his family, joyful. Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾, that is, would not return [al-Inshiqaq: 13–15]; ﴿Yes! Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾ [that is] (ziyadah from M): he struts, he is conceited. Qatadah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: he sways proudly.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾ This is a threat and a severe warning from Him, exalted is He, to the disbeliever who swaggers in his walk, that is: you deserve to walk like this, when you have disbelieved in your Creator and Originator, as is said in such a context by way of mockery and threat, like His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49], and like His saying: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals﴾ [al-Mursalat: 46], and like His saying: ﴿So worship what you wish besides Him﴾ [al-Zumar: 15], and like His saying: ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾ [Fussilat: 40], and other than that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾?" He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said it to Abu Jahl, then the Qur'an was revealed.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub narrated to us [[In M, A, H: "Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim"; the text is from Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (11638).]]. Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us (ḥ). And Abu Dawud narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it [[In M: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it to Abu Jahl."]], then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed it [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11638).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, from Ishaq, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾ It is a threat upon a threat, as you hear. And they claim that the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, seized the Prophet of Allah by the collar of his garments, then said: "Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!" The enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, said: Do you threaten me, O Muhammad? By Allah, neither you nor your Lord can do anything; indeed, I am the most honoured of those who walk between its two mountains.

* *

His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ al-Suddi said: that is, he will not be resurrected.

Mujahid, al-Shafi'i, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: that is, he will not be commanded nor forbidden.

The apparent meaning is that the verse covers both states: that is, he is not left in this world neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden, nor is he left in his grave neglected, not resurrected; rather he is commanded and forbidden in the world, and gathered to Allah in the Hereafter. The purpose here is to affirm the return, and to refute those among the people of deviation, ignorance and obstinacy who deny it. For this reason He said, reasoning from the origin to the return: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ That is: was not man a weak drop of despised water, emitted, poured out from the loins into the wombs? ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, so He created and proportioned﴾ That is: he became a clot, then a lump of flesh, then he was shaped, the soul was breathed into him, and he became another creation, complete and sound in his limbs, male or female, by Allah's permission and decree; for this reason He said: ﴿And He made of him two mates, the male and the female﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ That is: is not He who brought into being this complete creation from this weak drop able to restore him as He originated him? The power to restore is either by way of priority in relation to the origination, or equal according to the two opinions, in His saying: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

The first is more well-known, as explained previously in Surah al-Rum, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from another man: that he was on a rooftop reciting and raising his voice with the Qur'an, and when he recited: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, he said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, yes indeed." He was asked about that and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say it. Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: a man used to pray on top of his house, and whenever he recited: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, he said: "Glory be to You, yes indeed." They asked him about that and he said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Abu Dawud alone narrated this, and he did not name this Companion, and that does no harm.

Abu Dawud also said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Umayyah told me: I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you recites 'By the fig and the olive' and reaches its end: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, let him say: 'Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that.' And whoever recites 'Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection' and reaches: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, let him say: 'Yes.' And whoever recites 'By those sent forth' and reaches ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾, let him say: 'We believe in Allah.'"

Ahmad narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abi 'Umar, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (884), al-Musnad (2/249), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3347). The name of this Bedouin is given in a narration of al-Hakim, who narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/510) through Yazid ibn 'Iyad, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Abu al-Yasa', from Abu Hurayrah in similar wording, and said: "This ḥadīth has a sound chain but they did not record it." I say: Yazid ibn 'Iyad is a liar.]]. It was also narrated by Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, who said: I asked him: "Who narrated it to you?" He said: "A truthful man, from Abu Hurayrah" [[See Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi (11/105), where other supporting narrations are mentioned.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾: it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he recited it, would say: "Glory be to You, and yes" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/125).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Bateen, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he passed by this verse: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ and said: "Glory be to You; yes indeed."

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Qiyamah", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾: it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he recited it, would say: "Glory be to You, and yes" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/125).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Bateen, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he passed by this verse: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ and said: "Glory be to You; yes indeed."

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Qiyamah", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 75, verses 26–40:

He, exalted is He, informs about the state of the dying person and the terrors that accompany it; may Allah make us firm there by the firm word. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay! When it reaches the collarbones﴾. If we take ﴿Nay﴾ as a rebuke, its meaning is: O son of Adam, you will not deny there what you were told, rather it will become direct sight for you. If we take it to mean (ḥaqqan) "truly", it is clear: truly, when it reaches the collarbones, that is, when your soul is pulled out of your body and reaches your collarbones. The "tarāqī" (collarbones) is the plural of "tarqūwah" (collarbone), which are the bones between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder, as in His saying: ﴿Then why not, when it reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on? And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. Then why not, if you are not to be judged, you bring it back, if you should be truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Nay! When it reaches the collarbones﴾. And here the ḥadīth of Busr ibn Jaḥsh is mentioned, which was preceded in the commentary on Surah Yasin [[The ḥadīth of Busr ibn Jaḥsh, narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/310) through Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Busr ibn Jaḥsh: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spat one day into his palm, then placed his finger upon it, then said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: O son of Adam, do you think you can frustrate Me when I created you like this, until when I had proportioned you and balanced you, you walked between your two garments while the earth was yours to tread, then you gathered and withheld, until when the collarbones reached [the throat] you said: 'Shall I give charity? And when is the time for charity?!'" This was previously mentioned in the commentary on verse 77 of Surah Yasin.]]. The "tarāqī" is the plural of "tarqūwah", which is close to the throat (ḥulqūm).

﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, who is one who will perform ruqyah (incantation for healing)? Likewise Abu Qilabah said: ﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ meaning: who is a physician who can heal? Likewise said Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Rawh ibn al-Musayyib Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And it will be said: Who can cure?﴾ He said: It is said: who will ascend with his soul: the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment? According to this, it is from the speech of the angels.

With this same chain, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾ he said: the world and the Hereafter are wound around him. Likewise said Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾ says: the last day of the world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter, so hardship meets hardship, except for those whom Allah has mercy upon.

Ikrimah said: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾: a great matter with a great matter. Mujahid said: affliction with affliction. Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾, said: they are your two legs when they are wound together. In another narration from him: his two legs die and do not carry him, though he used to walk upon them. Likewise said al-Suddi, from Abu Malik.

In another narration from al-Hasan: it is the wrapping of the two of them in the shroud.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And leg is wound about leg﴾: two matters gather upon him: people prepare his body, and the angels prepare his soul.

* *

His saying: ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving﴾, that is, the return and the place of return. This is because the soul is raised to the heavens, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Return My servant to the earth, for from it I created them, into it I will return them, and from it I will bring them out once more." As occurs in the lengthy ḥadīth of al-Bara'. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ [al-An'am: 61–62].

* *

His saying: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away﴾ This is information about the disbeliever who, in the worldly life, denied the truth in his heart and turned away from acting with his body, so there is no good in him, inwardly or outwardly. For this reason He said: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾, that is: exultant, insolent, arrogant, lazy, having no resolve and no deed, as He said: ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 31]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, he was among his family, joyful. Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾, that is, would not return [al-Inshiqaq: 13–15]; ﴿Yes! Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾ [that is] (ziyadah from M): he struts, he is conceited. Qatadah and Zayd ibn Aslam said: he sways proudly.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾ This is a threat and a severe warning from Him, exalted is He, to the disbeliever who swaggers in his walk, that is: you deserve to walk like this, when you have disbelieved in your Creator and Originator, as is said in such a context by way of mockery and threat, like His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49], and like His saying: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals﴾ [al-Mursalat: 46], and like His saying: ﴿So worship what you wish besides Him﴾ [al-Zumar: 15], and like His saying: ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾ [Fussilat: 40], and other than that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾?" He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said it to Abu Jahl, then the Qur'an was revealed.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub narrated to us [[In M, A, H: "Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim"; the text is from Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (11638).]]. Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us (ḥ). And Abu Dawud narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it [[In M: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it to Abu Jahl."]], then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed it [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11638).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'ayb narrated to us, from Ishaq, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾ It is a threat upon a threat, as you hear. And they claim that the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, seized the Prophet of Allah by the collar of his garments, then said: "Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!" The enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, said: Do you threaten me, O Muhammad? By Allah, neither you nor your Lord can do anything; indeed, I am the most honoured of those who walk between its two mountains.

* *

His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ al-Suddi said: that is, he will not be resurrected.

Mujahid, al-Shafi'i, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: that is, he will not be commanded nor forbidden.

The apparent meaning is that the verse covers both states: that is, he is not left in this world neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden, nor is he left in his grave neglected, not resurrected; rather he is commanded and forbidden in the world, and gathered to Allah in the Hereafter. The purpose here is to affirm the return, and to refute those among the people of deviation, ignorance and obstinacy who deny it. For this reason He said, reasoning from the origin to the return: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ That is: was not man a weak drop of despised water, emitted, poured out from the loins into the wombs? ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, so He created and proportioned﴾ That is: he became a clot, then a lump of flesh, then he was shaped, the soul was breathed into him, and he became another creation, complete and sound in his limbs, male or female, by Allah's permission and decree; for this reason He said: ﴿And He made of him two mates, the male and the female﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ That is: is not He who brought into being this complete creation from this weak drop able to restore him as He originated him? The power to restore is either by way of priority in relation to the origination, or equal according to the two opinions, in His saying: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

The first is more well-known, as explained previously in Surah al-Rum, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from another man: that he was on a rooftop reciting and raising his voice with the Qur'an, and when he recited: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, he said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, yes indeed." He was asked about that and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say it. Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: a man used to pray on top of his house, and whenever he recited: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, he said: "Glory be to You, yes indeed." They asked him about that and he said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Abu Dawud alone narrated this, and he did not name this Companion, and that does no harm.

Abu Dawud also said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Umayyah told me: I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you recites 'By the fig and the olive' and reaches its end: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, let him say: 'Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that.' And whoever recites 'Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection' and reaches: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾, let him say: 'Yes.' And whoever recites 'By those sent forth' and reaches ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾, let him say: 'We believe in Allah.'"

Ahmad narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abi 'Umar, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (884), al-Musnad (2/249), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3347). The name of this Bedouin is given in a narration of al-Hakim, who narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/510) through Yazid ibn 'Iyad, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Abu al-Yasa', from Abu Hurayrah in similar wording, and said: "This ḥadīth has a sound chain but they did not record it." I say: Yazid ibn 'Iyad is a liar.]]. It was also narrated by Shu'bah, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, who said: I asked him: "Who narrated it to you?" He said: "A truthful man, from Abu Hurayrah" [[See Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi (11/105), where other supporting narrations are mentioned.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾: it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he recited it, would say: "Glory be to You, and yes" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (29/125).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim al-Bateen, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he passed by this verse: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ and said: "Glory be to You; yes indeed."

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Qiyamah", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
